applies_to: The SAME background opts work identically on ALL 4 slide-creating functions: addContent(html, opts), addQuiz(q, opts), addFillBlank(item, opts), addMatching(pairs, opts). Pass them in the shared `opts` object, alongside label/note/allowHTML (whichever of those apply to that function — see quiz.json/matching.json/fillinthegaps.json/content.json).
mechanism: There is a SINGLE shared <div id="slide-bg-layer"> element in the page (a sibling of #deck, position:fixed, never scrolls or transforms). updateBackgroundLayer() re-targets this ONE element every time the active slide changes (called from goTo()), reading that slide's opts. Slides with no `bg` in their opts simply hide the layer while active. This design exists specifically to avoid two earlier broken approaches (per-slide fixed pseudo-elements broke scroll during the swipe-transition transform; per-slide absolute pseudo-elements scrolled away with content instead of staying pinned) — never re-introduce a per-slide background element, always go through opts.bg on the shared layer.

opts_fields.bg: string, a path to an image (e.g. "./images/goroutines.jpg"). REQUIRED to activate a background at all — every other field below is ignored if `bg` is omitted. The image is pinned/fixed for the duration this slide is active; it does not scroll or pan with slide content.
opts_fields.overlayAlpha: number 0..1, default 0.5. A solid dark overlay drawn over the background image, purely for text legibility on top of it. 0 = no overlay (raw image), 1 = fully opaque (image invisible). Tune down for a subtle background, up for a busy/bright image behind lots of text.
opts_fields.backgroundSize: real CSS background-size value. "cover" = fills the whole slide, cropping overflow, keeps proportions (most common choice for photos). "contain" = fits the entire image inside the slide, may leave empty gaps, keeps proportions. "100% 100%" = stretches to exactly fill both dimensions, WILL distort non-matching aspect ratios. "100% auto" = fits width exactly, height scales proportionally (good for wide banner-shaped images). "auto" (default if omitted) = natural image size, no scaling at all — can leave most of the slide with no image showing for a small source image.
opts_fields.backgroundRepeat: real CSS background-repeat value. "no-repeat" (default) = shows the image once. "repeat" = tiles in both directions — use only with small seamless texture images, not photos. "repeat-x" / "repeat-y" = tiles along one axis only.
opts_fields.backgroundPosition: real CSS background-position value, default "top left". Common values: "center center", "top center", "bottom right", or percentages like "50% 50%". Controls which part of the image is anchored/visible when backgroundSize leaves extra space or crops.

minimal_example.note: overlayAlpha/backgroundSize/backgroundRepeat/backgroundPosition all fall back to their defaults (0.5, auto, no-repeat, top left) when omitted.

full_example.js:
addQuiz(questionObj, {
  bg: "./images/channels-diagram.png",
  overlayAlpha: 0.35,
  backgroundSize: "contain",
  backgroundRepeat: "no-repeat",
  backgroundPosition: "center center"
})
full_example.note: Lower overlayAlpha here because "contain" + a diagram image likely wants the image itself to stay legible/detailed, not darkened as heavily as a photo backdrop would need.

common_mistakes: Setting overlayAlpha/backgroundSize/etc without setting `bg` — they do nothing on their own, `bg` is the switch that turns the whole feature on for that slide.
Using "100% 100%" on a photo with a very different aspect ratio than the slide — this distorts/stretches the image; prefer "cover" for photos unless stretching is specifically wanted.

Forgetting that the background is a SHARED single element — if slide N has a bg and slide N+1 doesn't set one, it correctly disappears going forward; you never need to manually 'clear' a previous slide's background.
